# VAR ?= value assigns only if VAR is not already set: by the environment,
# the command line, or an earlier assignment. A plain = always assigns.
mk -p 1
stdout '^CC=gcc PREFIX=/usr/local X=first Y=y$'

# the environment can set a ?= variable, but not a = one
env CC=clang
env PREFIX=/opt
mk -p 1
stdout '^CC=clang PREFIX=/usr/local X=first Y=y$'

# the command line sets either kind
mk -p 1 CC=tcc PREFIX=/srv
stdout '^CC=tcc PREFIX=/srv X=first Y=y$'

# a skipped ?= is not evaluated, so its backquotes do not run
env SLOW=already
mk -p 1
! stderr 'evaluated'

-- mkfile --
CC ?= gcc
PREFIX = /usr/local
X = first
X ?= second
Y?=y
SLOW ?= `echo evaluated >&2`

show:V:
	echo CC=$CC PREFIX=$PREFIX X=$X Y=$Y
